description: OXYGENX is a team of two technology and space enthusiasts driven by curiosity, creativity, and innovation. We are passionate about software development, space exploration, Earth observation, and using technology to solve real-world challenges. We believe in learning, experimenting, and building ideas together. We welcome motivated collaborators with skills in data science, GIS, satellite imagery, UI/UX design, and scientific research who are excited to turn ideas into impact.
summary: Fire Atlas (team OXYGENX, NASA Space Apps 2026) is a satellite intelligence platform that corrects a severe bias in the historical monitoring of Caribbean fires. The arrival of the VIIRS satellite (375 m) in 2012 caused a false 426% increase in detections by fragmenting fires, breaking the climatic continuity with the previous satellite, MODIS (1 km). To solve this, Fire Atlas spatially and temporally fuses data from both sensors into a unified 1 km per day grid. Backed by a near-perfect Pearson correlation (r = 0.9923), the system applies a retrospective calibration factor (Cr) that statistically reconstructs the fires that MODIS missed between 2000 and 2011, achieving a continuous 27-year series. This science powers an interactive platform with real-time monitoring, historical percentile alerts, and automatic operational recommendations, directly impacting agricultural protection (SDG 2), climate action (SDG 13), and ecosystem conservation (SDG 15).
details:
WHAT IT DOES

FIRE ATLAS turns two incompatible NASA fire records into one continuous history for the Caribbean. MODIS (2000 onward) and VIIRS (2012 onward) differ in resolution, so raw counts rise sharply when VIIRS starts. Before 2012 we scale monthly MODIS counts by a per-territory factor estimated from the overlap period (for example Cuba 3.43, Dominican Republic 5.37, Haiti 6.96). From 2012 we fuse and de-duplicate both sensors (~1 km x 1 day). The result is a record where year-to-year changes reflect fire activity rather than the instrument.

FEATURES

- Harmonization simulator: raw vs harmonized series side by side.

- Burning calendar: seasonal percentile bands per territory and month.

- Recurrence map: historical detection density on a 0.1 degree grid, with polygon analysis.

- Live monitor: recent NASA FIRMS detections compared with the history of the same month. Alerts are comparisons, not forecasts.

WHY IT MATTERS

Anyone comparing Caribbean fire trends across 2012 without harmonizing sees a false +426% increase. Harmonizing gives a comparable baseline for planning and communication.

VALIDATION AND HONESTYScientific Validation:

Our methodology was rigorously validated using the Pearson correlation coefficient (r = 0.9923) across the 175-month overlap period (2012–2026) for the Caribbean territories. This confirmed a nearly perfect linear relationship between the raw MODIS data and our fused MODIS+VIIRS harmonized series, proving that both sensors track the exact same seasonal and climatic cycles. This statistical foundation justifies using our empirical Regional Calibration Factor (C_r) to accurately reconstruct the pre-2012 historical record.Known Limitations (Transparent Data):

To maintain absolute scientific integrity, we acknowledge that the series definition changes in 2012 (scaled MODIS before, fused multi-sensor after). We apply a single constant regional factor (C_r) per territory without a day/night split, and our metrics represent "1 km active fire fronts" (thermal anomalies) rather than isolated individual fires.

TOOLS

JavaScript, Leaflet and Leaflet.draw, Apache ECharts, Tailwind CSS, a Vercel serverless function (proxy that keeps the FIRMS key private), NASA FIRMS archive and API data. Source code: https://github.com/luisdrivera/fire-atlas-live

CREATIVITY

Instead of a new fire detector, we fixed the comparability problem underneath all fire trend analysis, and we published the limits next to the results.

AI USE

Claude (Anthropic), Gemini and GitHub Copilot assisted with code, data processing, documentation and slide creation. The team chose the method and direction and reviewed the outputs.
